# `common-cibseven-client` — autogenerated CIB seven REST client

A thin module that **generates** a typed Java client for the CIB seven engine REST API (`/engine-rest`)
at build time, consumed by `example-service` to drive the remote engine.

## Why generate instead of hand-writing (or using the community client)

- Hand-writing REST calls against `/engine-rest` is **error-prone**: URIs, the typed-variable payload
  (`{ "value": …, "type": … }`) and response shapes are all untyped strings/maps that only fail at
  runtime.
- The community REST client
  ([`cibseven-community-hub/cibseven-rest-client-java`](https://github.com/cibseven-community-hub/cibseven-rest-client-java))
  is **not actively maintained**, so it is not a safe dependency to build on.

Instead we generate the whole client from CIB seven's **official** OpenAPI document, so the client is
typed, complete and always matches the engine.

## How it works

The official spec ships as a bundled `openapi.json` inside the Maven artifact
`org.cibseven.bpm:cibseven-engine-rest-openapi`. The build (all in the `generate-sources` phase, see
this module's [`pom.xml`](pom.xml)):

1. resolves that artifact — pinned to the `cibseven.version` property in the root
   [`pom.xml`](../../pom.xml), so **client and engine never drift**;
2. extracts the bundled `openapi.json` into `target/openapi` (`maven-dependency-plugin`, `unpack`);
3. runs the [OpenAPI Generator](https://openapi-generator.tech) (`openapi-generator-maven-plugin`:
   `java` generator, `restclient` library — it builds on Spring's `RestClient`, matching how the worker
   talks to the engine; Spring Boot 4, Jackson 3, Jakarta EE, JSpecify) to generate the full client
   under `target/generated-sources/openapi`;
4. compiles the generated sources into this module.

Nothing generated is committed — it is a build artifact under `target/` and is regenerated on every
build. To bump the API, bump `cibseven.version`.

The generated packages consumers use:

- `org.cibseven.rest.client.api.*` — one `…Api` class per tag (e.g. `MessageApi`, `TaskApi`,
  `DeploymentApi`, `ProcessDefinitionApi`, …). Each is constructed from an `ApiClient`
  (`org.cibseven.rest.client.ApiClient`), which wraps a Spring `RestClient`. Operations take a single
  **request object** (`useSingleRequestParameter=static`) where they have many parameters — e.g.
  `taskApi.getTasks(new TaskApi.GetTasksRequest().processInstanceBusinessKey(key))` instead of ~100
  positional query parameters.
- `org.cibseven.rest.client.model.*` — the request/response DTOs (e.g. `CorrelationMessageDto`,
  `CompleteTaskDto`, `VariableValueDto`), mutable POJOs with fluent setters.

> **Mind the base path:** the generated `ApiClient` builds absolute URLs from its **own** `basePath`
> (default `http://localhost:8080/engine-rest`) and ignores the `RestClient`'s `baseUrl` — always
> create it as `new ApiClient(restClient).setBasePath(engineBaseUrl)`.

## Using it (see `example-service`)

`ExampleServiceApplication` builds one `RestClient` pointed at the engine base URL, wraps it in an
`ApiClient` with the same base path, and exposes the `…Api` beans from it; `RemoteLeasingProcessAdapter`
injects `MessageApi` / `TaskApi` and calls typed methods instead of hand-built REST.

> **One exception:** `POST /deployment/create` is a multipart upload of *several* files with dynamic
> filenames, which the spec models as a single binary field — the generated client cannot faithfully
> express it, so `ProcessModelDeploymentAdapter` deliberately stays on a hand-built `RestClient`.
